notes:
**Twenty sentences a person would actually type, run through the parser. Five came back confidently wrong.**

**"delta 0.4 crosses above 0.5" was read as EMA 4 crossing EMA 0** - and shown in the green half as understood. The cross pattern was matching the digits either side of the decimal point. "price 0.5 crosses 1.5" came back as EMA 5 crossing EMA 1 with nothing in the amber box at all. An EMA now needs the word ema actually present, and a period of 0, 1, or one equal to the other is refused.

**"rsi 30 kinda unte konu, 70 paiki vellithe ammu" was flipped to SHORT.** Buy below 30, sell above 70 - and because the sentence contains a sell word the whole rule faced the wrong way and would have SOLD when RSI fell below 30. Which way a rule faces is decided by the first clause that names an action now.

**"... buy, ... sell" put both halves in the ENTRY.** Cross above AND cross below on the same bar, joined with AND: a rule that can never fire, read back as two conditions understood perfectly. Each clause now knows its own side, whether the verb leads it or trails it.

**Telugu never reached the parser at all.** The translator existed and only the AI path used it. So a Telugu sentence the app can read perfectly was declared unreadable and sent to a paid model. It now comes in the same door as English - free, instant, offline.

Also: "1 percent stop" is now a stop (it was silently keeping the default half-percent), and "before 3 pm" is now read - the time gate only worked in one direction.
